elements.content: Rain rattles the skylight. Old consoles hum under emergency power.
ARIA threads a tape reel while NOAH coaxes a signal out of a battered mixer.
JUNE covers a whiteboard with road closures, shelter names, and call signs.
KELL rushes in carrying a portable antenna, a dented lantern, and a canvas tool bag.
Bridge is closed. Cell towers are dead. The hill relay is our only shot.
Please tell me that antenna is less cursed than it looks.
It only tried to kill me once.
Good. Tonight we don't have time for a second opinion.
Aria flips a switch. The ON AIR sign flickers, then dies again.
Give me ten minutes and one miracle.

data.heading: INT. COMMUNITY RADIO STUDIO - NIGHT

narrative_beats.description: The studio is introduced under emergency power during a storm, with the team each performing a distinct role — threading tape, coaxing signals, mapping closures — establishing the crisis context and ensemble dynamic.
Kell arrives with the portable antenna and delivers the key logistical problem: the bridge is closed, cell towers are dead, and the hill relay is the only option.

The exchange about the antenna ('It only tried to kill me once') and June's deadpan response ('Tonight we don't have time for a second opinion') pairs genuine danger with dry banter, undercutting urgency with gallows humor.
Aria flips the switch and the ON AIR sign flickers and dies, making the broadcast goal feel precarious and unresolved.
Aria asks for ten minutes and a miracle; June's reply ('Take fifteen. Keep the miracle.') reframes the impossible as manageable, ending the scene on wry solidarity.

data.tone_mood: tense urgency undercut by dry, gallows humor
tone_shifts: Opens in atmospheric dread (rain, emergency power, dead infrastructure) then shifts toward dark comedy as the team's banter deflates the danger without dismissing it.
